newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil traders say possible China bought soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Brazil traders say possible China bought soybeans.

text.p: Brazilian traders could not confirm talk that China bought 50,000 to 100,000 tonnes Brazilian soybeans for June-July delivery over the last three days, but said such a sale was likely at current prices.
"Premiums (for soybeans) were very strong at the end of last week which gives to understand something is being done. There is something to it," said David Brew, trader at Brasoja.
Rumors of China buying South American soybeans and meal began to surface earlier as the Chicago market reopened after being closed Monday for U.S. Memorial Day, a trader said.

Dealers said it was likely that any soybean sale would have been shared between Brazil and Argentina, as the latter could more easily ship the product and was highly eager to sell, having possibly missed out on the peak in prices.

"It's not impossible that they bought June but I would say it's rather difficult," said one soymeal trader. "It's more probably they would get it from Argentina or (the southern port of) Rio Grande do Sul or any other port than Paranagua."
He noted it would be difficult to get a new vessel to leave Paranagua, Brazil's main grain loading port, before the end of June unless a vessel was already in position.

"We're going to see all the demand is going to be turning to Brazil and Argentina now," said Brew. "We're going to be selling everything now -- we have to, the price is right." ((--Joelle Diderich, Sao Paulo newsroom +55 11 248 5417))
